methodology: Official GitHub repository metadata and upstream documentation. Six non-archived candidates, two archived exclusions; four selected by direct learning fit, not stars alone. No software was installed or executed.

candidates.reason: A mature spaced-repetition program for a small personal English/Japanese card workflow; choose it for repeatable review and editable note structure, not as a promise of exam success.
candidates.starter_task: Define a personal note type and inspect a 12-row original bilingual TSV fixture before any import. Map fields, retain stable record IDs, and design a Markdown export for the second brain.
acceptance_criteria: All 12 fixture rows have unique record IDs and all required fields.
An import trial into a disposable test deck preserves the IDs and handles a repeated import without unintended duplication; this runtime test remains pending.
A future Markdown export preserves expression, reading, self-authored example, source, and actual creation date.
No private performance history or copyrighted deck is placed in the public fork.

candidates.reason: Reserve: a useful general ebook reader, but the first batch prioritizes language-specific review, lookup, reading logs, and listening.
Reserve: investigate scheduling only after a stable basic review routine; avoid algorithm tuning as a substitute for language practice.
A language-focused browser dictionary project suited to Japanese reading and a later Anki field mapping; lower stars than general readers but closer to the stated Japanese goal.
candidates.starter_task: Review a proposed dictionary-to-card field contract using six original Japanese examples. Compare the contract with the current official Anki integration documentation before producing real extension settings.
acceptance_criteria: Expression, reading, own example, source URL, and source date have distinct fields.
Dictionary definitions and audio retain their separate licensing and provenance; none are bundled in this fixture.
Repeated captures of the same example have an explicit deduplication key.
The JSON contract is labelled a study specification, not importable Yomitan settings.

candidates.reason: Excluded from the active shortlist because the repository is archived.
A language-reading tool suited to tracking comprehension, unknown terms, and summaries alongside an Obsidian note; selected for direct learning fit rather than popularity alone.
candidates.starter_task: Design a reading-log-to-Markdown contract using two original miniature texts and a CSV fixture. Keep reading evidence separate from proposed lesson completion.
acceptance_criteria: The English and Japanese text samples are explicitly self-authored and carry unique IDs.
Each reading-log row links a text ID, own summary, terms to review, and a status.
A future export handles punctuation, Unicode, empty observations, and repeat runs without silently overwriting a private note.
Actual reading time and scores remain blank until measured.

candidates.reason: A focused subtitle and sentence-mining project for small listening exercises; the current canonical repository is asbplayer/asbplayer, redirected from killergerbah/asbplayer.
candidates.starter_task: Use a four-cue original SRT and a provenance manifest to design a short listening-to-card workflow. Record a matching original audio/video clip later; no media has been produced or imported by this task.
acceptance_criteria: SRT cue numbers are sequential and times are monotonic and non-overlapping.
The manifest explicitly states that this is a text-only fixture with no recorded media yet.
Every future card can be traced to a clip ID, cue, source rights, and actual learning date.
A real playback/import test is documented only after it is executed.

candidates.reason: Excluded from the active shortlist because the repository is archived.
